back: $T = \dfrac{\lambda x}{l}$: tension (or thrust) $T$, modulus $\lambda$ (N), extension (or compression) $x$, natural length $l$.

front: Work done stretching from extension x₁ to x₂

back: The constant λ (in newtons) in T = λx/l: the tension that would double the natural length; depends on the material, not the length.
A string can only be in tension (slack below natural length, no EPE); a spring can also be compressed and push with a thrust.

front: Greatest speed on an elastic string or spring
back: Where the acceleration is zero: tension equals weight (the equilibrium position).

front: Method for motion on a taut elastic string
back: Conservation of energy: KE + GPE + EPE = constant (no suvat: the force varies).

front: Equilibrium of a particle between two elastic strings in a line
back: The tensions are equal; the two extensions add up to the gap minus the natural lengths.
